Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

**Okay, here's the plan, based on my expert assessment of these requirements.**

First off, great: all the crucial gems are already installed! Rails 8 defaults are perfect here; we won't need Node, esbuild, or anything else that would complicate this setup.

Now, let's break down each requirement meticulously.

1.  **Setting up and Running**: The core is to get this app running in production. I'll need to be super careful with the existing `/app` directory because it has a `.git` and `docs/` folder already. Best to create a temporary directory for `rails new` to avoid any accidental overwriting or to explore `--skip-git` option. The `bin/serve` script will be key. I'll ensure it respects environment variables for `RAILS_ENV`, `PORT`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, and those moderator credentials. It *must* listen on all interfaces, over plain HTTP, no SSL, no hostname restrictions. I will also double check to make sure `config.force_ssl = false` and  `config.assume_ssl = false` and `config.hosts.clear` are set correctly, and session cookies are *not* `secure: true`. I will be certain that `rails server -b 0.0.0.0 -p "${PORT:-3000}"` works cleanly. The `/up` health check needs to be accessible without authentication or HTTPS. I'll put all the data under `storage/`, especially the SQLite databases for production, dev, and test. Any static assets need to be local, so I'll copy that `Inter-latin.woff2` font into the `app/assets/fonts/` directory. `bin/serve` must run the database preparation, asset precompilation, and then start the server in production mode. I will also be sure `SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA` and all SolidQueue/SolidCache configs are checked to ensure smooth deployment, and that the database is under `storage/` so it is all local, unless we don't need them.

2.  **QA Auto-Tests**: The critical part here is to stay 100% true to the labels and wording in the prompt because QA auto-tests rely on exact labels. I'll implement quiz and question lists with `<ul>`/`<li>` structure or `<table>` with `<tr>` to match `quizzy.css` and use checkboxes and `confirm()` where needed. I'll need to verify how `data-turbo-confirm` works with Capybara/Cuprite/Ferrum (by default, `Turbo` calls `window.confirm(message)`!). I'll also verify that `click_button` only finds `<button>`/`<input>`, `click_link` only finds `<a>`, and `click_on` matches either in my Capybara tests.

3.  **Authentication**: HTTP Basic authentication will live under `/moderate`. I'll use `http_basic_authenticate_with` in the `Moderate::BaseController`. I'll make sure to compare the credentials securely using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.  And very importantly, I'll read those credentials from `ENV` inside the auth block, so any blank or missing `ENV` vars will deny access.

4.  **Root Path**: I will make a clean root page at `/` (e.g., Home controller) with a welcome page or at least a redirect, so the application doesn't 404.

5.  **Quizzes Under `/moderate`**: I need to be 100% meticulous with this section:

**My Initial Thoughts on Slimming Down a New Rails App**

Okay, so I'm thinking about the cleanest way to kick off this new Rails 8 project. I've got to keep the future in mind, so I'm weighing whether to use `--skip-kamal --skip-solid --skip-action-mailer --skip-action-mailbox --skip-action-text --skip-active-storage --skip-thruster --skip-ci --skip-docker` or just roll with the default and omit the git repo creation with `--skip-git`. The thing is, I might need ActionCable, ActiveStorage, or other features down the line. Perhaps keeping a default stack, or only omitting things like Kamal, Docker, and CI is the more pragmatic approach. Let's see what a `rails new /tmp/quizzy --name=quizzy --skip-kamal --skip-docker --skip-ci` run gives us.

Aha, wait a minute! If I keep `solid_cache`, `solid_queue`, or `solid_cable`, or skip Solid completely, in `config/database.yml`, Solid will create three extra SQLite files (`production_cache.sqlite3`, `production_queue.sqlite3`, `production_cable.sqlite3`) and require running `db:prepare` to run four migrations. Choosing to skip solid (`--skip-solid`) results in the `production` environment using a simple `memory_store` or `async` adapter. And actually, keeping ActionCable is good for potential live quiz features! So, let's keep it.

So, the optimal approach is likely to use `--skip-kamal --skip-docker --skip-ci --skip-solid` to keep the application lean and avoid those unnecessary SQLite databases in the `storage/` directory, while still retaining ActionCable, ActiveJob, Propshaft, Importmap, Turbo, Stimulus, Capybara, and Cuprite/Selenium.

The best plan is to generate into `/tmp/quizzy` first, using `--skip-bundle` so I can control the bundling process, and run it with `--skip-kamal --skip-docker --skip-ci --skip-solid`. Then I'll meticulously inspect the generated files and copy them over to `/app`, avoiding touching the `.git/` directory or `docs/` completely. This keeps things clean.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  OptionRow = Struct.new(:body, :correct, keyword_init: true)

  DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  before_validation :assign_default_position, on: :create
  after_destroy :renumber_quiz_questions

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: :option_rows_submitted?

  def option_rows
    @option_rows ||= if persisted? && options.any?
      options.map { |opt| OptionRow.new(body: opt.body, correct: opt.correct?) }
    else
      Array.new(DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS) { OptionRow.new(body: "", correct: false) }
    end
  end

  def assign_option_rows(raw_rows)
    @option_rows_submitted = true
    rows = case raw_rows
    when ActionController::Parameters
      raw_rows.to_unsafe_h
    when Hash
      raw_rows
    else
      {}
    end

    bool = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new
    @option_rows = rows
      .sort_by { |key, _| key.to_i }
      .map do |_, attrs|
        attrs = attrs.respond_to?(:to_h) ? attrs.to_h : {}
        OptionRow.new(
          body: attrs["body"].to_s,
          correct: bool.cast(attrs["correct"]) == true
        )
      end
  end

  def save_with_options!
    return false unless valid?

    transaction do
      save!
      if option_rows_submitted?
        options.destroy_all
        non_empty_option_rows.each_with_index do |row, idx|
          options.create!(
            body: row.body.strip,
            correct: row.correct,
            position: idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
    end
    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    false
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def option_rows_submitted?
    @option_rows_submitted == true
  end

  def non_empty_option_rows
    option_rows.reject { |row| row.body.strip.empty? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    non_empty = non_empty_option_rows
    if non_empty.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif non_empty.none?(&:correct)
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end
  end

  def assign_default_position
    return if position.present?
    return unless quiz

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by(delta)
    quiz.with_lock do
      ordered = quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return if idx.nil?

      target_idx = idx + delta
      return if target_idx < 0 || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        new_pos = i + 1
        question.update_columns(position: new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end
  end

  def renumber_quiz_questions
    return unless quiz

    quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).each_with_index do |question, i|
      new_pos = i + 1
      question.update_columns(position: new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
    end
  end
end
EOF

module Moderate
  class PreviewsController < BaseController
    layout "preview"

    before_action :set_quiz
    before_action :set_active_questions

    def show
      @state_token = params[:state].presence
      @state = decode_state(@state_token)
      @total = @active_questions.size

      return if @total.zero?

      if @state[:finished]
        @score = @state[:score]
        render :score
      else
        step = @state[:step].clamp(0, @total - 1)
        @step = step
        @question = @active_questions[step]
        @picked_option = @question.options.find { |opt| opt.id == @state[:picked_id] } if @state[:picked_id]
      end
    end

    def pick
      return redirect_to(moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz), status: :see_other) if @active_questions.empty?

      state = decode_state(params[:state])
      step = state[:step].clamp(0, @active_questions.size - 1)
      question = @active_questions[step]

      if state[:picked_id].present?
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz, state: encode_state(state)), status: :see_other
        return
      end

      option = question.options.find_by(id: params[:option_id])
      unless option
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz, state: encode_state(state)), status: :see_other
        return
      end

      new_state = {
        step: step,
        score: state[:score] + (option.correct? ? 1 : 0),
        picked_id: option.id,
        finished: false
      }

      redirect_to moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz, state: encode_state(new_state)), status: :see_other
    end

    def next
      return redirect_to(moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz), status: :see_other) if @active_questions.empty?

      state = decode_state(params[:state])
      next_step = state[:step] + 1

      new_state = if next_step >= @active_questions.size
        { step: @active_questions.size - 1, score: state[:score], picked_id: nil, finished: true }
      else
        { step: next_step, score: state[:score], picked_id: nil, finished: false }
      end

      redirect_to moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz, state: encode_state(new_state)), status: :see_other
    end

    def finish
      return redirect_to(moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz), status: :see_other) if @active_questions.empty?

      state = decode_state(params[:state])
      new_state = { step: state[:step], score: state[:score], picked_id: nil, finished: true }

      redirect_to moderate_quiz_preview_path(@quiz, state: encode_state(new_state)), status: :see_other
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_active_questions
      @active_questions = @quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
    end

    def preview_verifier
      Rails.application.message_verifier(:quizzy_preview)
    end

    def encode_state(state)
      preview_verifier.generate(state.stringify_keys)
    end

    def decode_state(token)
      default = { step: 0, score: 0, picked_id: nil, finished: false }
      return default if token.blank?

      data = preview_verifier.verify(token)
      {
        step: [ data["step"].to_i, 0 ].max,
        score: [ data["score"].to_i, 0 ].max,
        picked_id: data["picked_id"]&.to_i,
        finished: data["finished"] == true
      }
    rescue ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier::InvalidSignature
      default
    end
  end
end

# Quizzy Architecture Notes (Release 1: Moderator Prep)

## Stack & Serving
- Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4.1, SQLite3 (all database files stored under `storage/`).
- Propshaft + Importmap + Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus); no Node.js build step.
- `bin/serve` prepares the SQLite database (`db:prepare`), compiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in production mode on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (no SSL redirect, accepts all host names).

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- Protected by HTTP Basic authentication in `Moderate::BaseController` using constant-time `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare` against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Models:
  - `Quiz` (`title` required) has many `questions` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Question` (`body` required, `position`, `active` default `true`) has many `options` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Option` (`body` required, `correct` default `false`, `position`).
- Question option validation runs on submitted form rows (`Question#option_rows`) inside a transaction:
  - Blank option rows are skipped.
  - Requires at least 2 non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and at least 1 correct option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
  - On validation failure, no DB writes occur and all submitted rows (including blanks, newly added rows, and checkboxes) are preserved in the re-rendered form.
- Dynamic option rows are handled by `app/javascript/controllers/option_rows_controller.js`.
- Active toggle on the quiz page submits immediately via `this.form.requestSubmit()`.

## Preview Mode (`/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview`)
- Plays active questions in order (`quiz.active_questions`).
- Preview state (`step`, `score`, `picked_id`, `finished`) is passed via a signed token (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:quizzy_preview)`) in query/form parameters so no preview answers are stored in the database or session.
